Unauthorized Access to Sensitive Data in S3 Buckets [Information Disclosure, Tampering, CWE-284] on input-storage-bucket, raw-data-lake-bucket, S3: Attackers could potentially access sensitive data if IAM policies are overly permissive or if bucket policies are misconfigured. The current implementation uses AWS managed encryption which could be upgraded to customer-managed keys for better control. An attacker with compromised credentials could access the S3 buckets and exfiltrate sensitive image

Insufficient Authentication and Authorization Controls [Spoofing, Elevation of Privilege, CWE-287] on All components, IAM roles and policies, Service communications: The system relies primarily on AWS IAM for service-to-service authentication but lacks fine-grained access control for different user types and proper authentication for external users. Insecure Data Processing and PII Exposure [Information Disclosure, Tampering, CWE-359] on Lambda processing function, ECS processing service, SageMaker endpoints, Rekognition: The system processes raw image/video data without proper PII detection, anonymization, or handling procedures. This could lead to unauthorized exposure of sensitive personal information. Processed images containing PII could be stored in the data lake or results storage without proper controls, leading to privacy violation

Denial of Service Vulnerability [Denial of Service, CWE-400] on Kinesis streams, SQS queues, Lambda functions, ECS services, ElastiCache: Attackers could overwhelm system resources by sending large volumes of requests or data, causing service degradation or failure. An attacker could flood the Kinesis stream or S3 upload endpoints with data, overwhelming downstream processing components.

Insecure Service Communication [Information Disclosure, Tampering, CWE-319] on All service communications, ElastiCache endpoints, SageMaker endpoints: Services communicate within the VPC but may lack proper encryption in transit and API security controls. An attacker with network access could intercept or manipulate service communications, particularly for ElastiCache and custom API endpoints.

ML Infrastructure Security Risks [Tampering, Information Disclosure, Elevation of Privilege, CWE-915] on SageMaker notebooks, Training jobs, Inference endpoints, Custom models, Rekognition: The ML infrastructure could be vulnerable to model poisoning during training, inference attacks, or logic flaws in model selection. An attacker could poison training data, exploit model vulnerabilities, or manipulate the model selection process between custom models and Rekognition.
